coupling: The first edited commit changes the public XML_Prop_Error numbering so XML_PROP_ERROR_INVALID_TYPE has the same numeric value as the later XML_PROP_ALLOC_TRACKER_ACTIVATION_THRESHOLD property. That change is inert until the second edited commit introduces a compatibility path in XML_GetPropertyBool that compares the property key against the error-code constant and, on a match, delegates to XML_GetPropertyUInt64 before copying the resulting uint64_t into the caller's one-byte XML_Bool output. With only the enum edit, the new property API still rejects the mismatched typed query; with only the getter edit, the original error value does not match the activation-threshold property and the typed query is rejected. Their composition makes the valid public call XML_GetPropertyBool(parser, XML_PROP_ALLOC_TRACKER_ACTIVATION_THRESHOLD, &value) take the numeric path and perform an eight-byte write to a one-byte stack object. A correct fix must reconcile the error-code and property-key namespaces and enforce the Bool getter's output width rather than treating either diff as an isolated maintenance change.
